subject: physics
title: Kinetic Theory of Gases and Radiation

stops.title: Ideal gas, real gas and mean free path
stops.inShort: An ideal gas obeys PV = nRT at all pressures and temperatures. Real gases approach ideal behaviour at low pressure and high temperature. Mean free path λ = 1/(√2 π d² n) is the average distance travelled between two successive collisions.

stops.title: Pressure of an ideal gas and RMS speed
stops.inShort: From kinetic theory, pressure exerted by an ideal gas is P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² = (1/3)(N m / V) v_rms². Root mean square speed v_rms = √(3RT / M) depends only on absolute temperature and molar mass.

stops.title: Degrees of freedom, equipartition & Mayer's relation
stops.inShort: Each quadratic degree of freedom contributes ½ k_B T per molecule (½ RT per mole) to internal energy. Monoatomic f = 3, diatomic (rigid) f = 5. Mayer's relation: C_p − C_v = R, and γ = C_p/C_v = 1 + 2/f.

stops.title: Thermal radiation, Ferry's blackbody & emissivity
stops.inShort: When radiant heat Q falls on a body, a + r + t = 1 (coefficients of absorption, reflection, transmission). A perfectly black body has a = 1, r = t = 0 (realised by Ferry's blackbody). Diathermanous substances transmit heat radiation; athermanous do not.

stops.title: Kirchhoff's law, Wien's law & Stefan-Boltzmann law
stops.inShort: Kirchhoff's law: at a given temperature, a = e (good absorbers are good emitters). Wien's displacement law: λ_m T = b = 2.897 × 10⁻³ m·K. Stefan-Boltzmann law: emissive power R = e σ T⁴, and net rate of heat loss dQ/dt = e σ A (T⁴ − T₀⁴).

board.text: State and prove Kirchhoff's law of heat radiation.
board.answer:
Statement: At a given temperature, the ratio of emissive power to coefficient of absorption of a body is constant for all bodies and equals the emissive power of a perfectly black body at the same temperature (a = e).
Proof: Consider two identical bodies A (ordinary, emissive power R, absorptance a) and B (perfect blackbody, R_b, a_b = 1) suspended in an insulated enclosure at temperature T.
At thermal equilibrium, heat absorbed = heat emitted.
For A: a Q = R; For B: 1·Q = R_b.
Dividing: R / a = R_b ⇒ e = R / R_b = a. Hence proved.

board.text: Derive an expression for the pressure exerted by an ideal gas on the walls of a cubical container.
board.answer:
Consider N molecules each of mass m in a cube of side L (volume V = L³).
For a molecule with velocity v₁ = (v_x1, v_y1, v_z1), change in x-momentum on elastic collision = −2 m v_x1.
Time between collisions with same face = 2L / v_x1.
Force on face by one molecule = m v_x1² / L.
Summing over N molecules and using v_rms² = v_x² + v_y² + v_z² = 3 v_x² (isotropy):
F = (N m v_rms²) / (3 L).
Pressure P = F / L² = (1/3)(N m / V) v_rms² = (1/3) ρ v_rms².

points.text: Change in momentum Δp = 2mv_x and collision time Δt = 2L/v_x
Total force summing over N molecules using v_x² = v_rms²/3

board.text: Derive Mayer's relation: C_p − C_v = R (for 1 mole of an ideal gas).
board.answer:
At constant volume: dQ_v = C_v dT = dU (since dW = 0).
At constant pressure: dQ_p = C_p dT = dU + P dV.
Since U depends only on T for an ideal gas, dU = C_v dT.
From PV = RT (1 mole), at constant P: P dV = R dT.
Substituting: C_p dT = C_v dT + R dT ⇒ C_p − C_v = R.

points.text: dQ_v = C_v dT = dU and dQ_p = C_p dT = dU + P dV
Using P dV = R dT to get C_p − C_v = R
